# screen_wedge

<!-- AUTO: regenerated by `nurb card`. Do not hand-edit. -->
Size: 126.10 x 77.80 x 19.60 mm, 52728.7 mm3, 1 solid, 136 faces
Checks: 1 finding: 1 warn (overhang)
<!-- /AUTO -->

```toml
[part]
material = "PLA"
min_wall = 0.6
```

**PLA, and it is the only PLA part in the project.** Everything else is PETG: the
chassis runs 40–50 °C and the top plate a little more, which is where PLA starts to
creep under sustained load. This part is the exception on purpose — it is the visible
one, and **ironing the top face** is a finish PETG cannot produce. The machine runs
10–15 min twice a day and is at room temperature the rest of the time, so the wedge
never reaches thermal equilibrium; it also sits highest in the stack, above
`screen_base` and its 5 mm standoff grid. The thing to watch is that the 5 V supply
lives in `screen_base` directly underneath and heat rises: if the frame ever warps,
the answer is PETG and no ironing.

## What it is

Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-4.3 carrier: open rear **frame** on the bed, solid border skirt, module pocket cut straight through it. The module drops in from the front and its own four M2.5 standoffs land on four seat pads; M2.5 screws come up from under the bed face and thread into those standoffs. The skirt's own top face is the frame, level with the glass. Outer size is glass + 10 mm sides + 5 mm top/bottom.

The rear plate is a frame exactly the width of the seat pads (`rear_frame_margin` 0), notched out to the pocket wall in front of the JST connectors on the edge opposite USB-C, so the whole back of the module is reachable and every connector can be plugged perpendicular to the PCB. USB-C and UART channels punch through the outer +X face as well as the rear plate, so the plugs can be reached from the side once a wrapping base hides the skirt.

## Design notes

- Print pose: **rear plate on the bed**, solid skirt rising, **frame rim on top**. The skirt is one volume with the pocket cut through it — not a separate inner wall.
- `pocket_depth` 12.8 mm runs from the pad tops to the rim: 8.80 glass-to-PCB plus the module's own 4.00 mm standoffs. The pads carry the standoffs, not the PCB, so leaving the standoffs out of the sum puts the frame 4.3 mm below the glass.
- **Screws are M2.5×8, and the length is not a free choice.** The counterbore is `counterbore(2.9, 4.9, 2.7, seat_z)`, so the head bears at z = 2.70 and the pad top is at z = `rear_wall + seat_height` = 6.80: **4.10 mm of plastic to cross**. An M2.5×8 therefore takes **3.90 mm** of the module's 4.00 mm standoff — 1.56 × D of engagement with 0.10 mm to spare, so it clamps rather than bottoming out even if the standoff's thread is blind. M2.5×6 would give 1.90 mm (0.76 × D), under the 1 × D minimum; M2.5×10 overshoots by 2.10 mm. Nothing standard sits between 6 and 8.
- `seat_height` is **4.3, not 4.0, for that reason**: at 4.0 the crossing is 3.80 mm and an M2.5×8 wants 4.20 mm of a 4.00 mm standoff. The drawing gives the standoff's height and says nothing about its thread depth, so 4.0 was betting on a through-threaded standoff. The 0.3 mm buys the part out of that bet; it costs 0.3 mm of overall height and 1.3 % of volume.
- The channels are roofed by the PCB's own back plane (`rim_z - module_glass_to_pcb`), because the sockets hang under the board. Stopping them at the seat plane leaves them 4 mm below the sockets.
- Build order matters: **volumes, then pocket and rear opening, then the seat pads, then the channels and counterbores**. Adding the pads before the pocket cut is what made them vanish for three sessions; cutting the channels before the pads left a 0.1 mm tongue across one.
- Seat pads are rectangular and flush into the pocket corners. A round pad leaves a wedge of void against the corner too thin to print.
- **The rear plate is a frame the width of the pads, and the 1 mm of overhang it used to keep around them was retired on purpose.** The pads take their strength from the skirt: two of their four faces are fused into the pocket wall, which is 9.5 mm thick there. The doctrine's "a loaded hole earns a fastener diameter of wall" is about the **Ø2.9 bore**, and the pad already gives exactly 2.50 mm on its two free faces without the plate's help. The plate around the **Ø4.9 head pocket** carries nothing at all: the pocket runs z 0 → 2.70, *below* the shoulder the head bears on, and the loaded material is the 4.10 mm of column between that shoulder and the pad top, in pure compression, fused into the skirt. The thread is in the module's metal standoff, so the split-the-boss failure the rule guards against cannot happen here. Flush therefore leaves **1.50 mm** around the head pocket, which was already the number between z 2.50 and 2.70 where the pocket mords into the pad — flush extends an existing minimum rather than creating one. The 1 mm of overhang cost 701 mm³ for nothing. `rear_frame_margin` is the slider that buys it back, and `reject` stops it going under 1.2 mm.
- **The frame also narrowed the USB-C side strip, 16.55 → 8.50 mm, and `outer_wall` 0 then notched that strip at the two channels.** At the channels' own y the rear plate is now only the 8.25 mm inner strip (x 45.05 → 53.30); the 2.65 mm that used to sit outside the channel is gone so the openings reach the outer face. Between and around the two openings the plate still ties the skirt. Each millimetre of `rear_frame_margin` puts a millimetre straight back; `outer_wall` puts the leftover wall back. Slices clean. The number to watch if the part ever feels flexy at the plug.
- **The connector window runs to the pocket wall, and a bigger rear opening cannot replace it.** The pads sit in the pocket corners, i.e. on the *same band as the PCB edge*, so a frame cut to them still leaves 9.00 mm of plate measured in from the module edge — and the connectors live in the first 5–6 mm of it. Enlarging the opening only shortens the notch, 16.55 → 8.25 mm; it never opens it. The notch is 8.25 × 44.00, from the frame's lip out to x −53.30, and it cannot go further: beyond the pocket wall is the 9.5 mm rail that ties the skirt to the rear plate on that side.
- **The window covers 41 mm, not the 31 mm the three signal connectors need.** The extra 10 mm reaches the battery connector at the bottom — not because it has to be plugged, but because it is the tall one and a plate over it is a plate it could foul. `connector_window_margin` 1.5 adds to each end, so the cut is y −21.10 to +22.90 and a caliper reading off by a millimetre still misses every latch.
- **The window is on the edge opposite USB-C, and `nurb diff` cannot catch a mirror.** Same trap as the cable relief. The check is the bed face's centroid in `nurb inspect`: it reads **x +1.53** because the material removed sits at −x (the through USB channels at +x pull it back from the old +2.33). On the wrong side it would read about −6.
- **Pad size is a fight with the UART channel, not a free choice.** The UART socket is 12.93 mm from the top edge and the screw 4.00 mm from it: 8.93 mm between centres, and both the pad and the plug want it. The pads are therefore sized to the doctrine minimum — 2.5 mm of material around the Ø2.9 bore, so `pad_y` 8.35 and `pad_x` 8.25 — and nothing more. The old square 9.0 mm pad reached y 25.40 while the bare socket ends at y 25.47: **it was touching the connector with 0.07 mm to spare**, and the 14.5 mm channel then cut across it, which is the pad-in-front-of-the-opening the viewer showed. Today the pad starts at y 26.05 and the channel ends at 25.77: **0.28 mm**. That is the tightest number in the part, and `reject` on `cable_slot_width` guards it.
- `seat_height` must stay above 3.2 mm: `counterbore` stacks two 1 mm bridging steps over the 2.7 mm head bore, and the pad needs solid material above them.
- Nothing inside the pocket below **the PCB's back plane** is chamfered (`buried`) — the module covers it and the chamfers only made slivers there. The ceiling is `pcb_back_z` (10.80) and not `seat_z` (6.80) because the two channel mouths rise to exactly that plane and are just as hidden. At `seat_z` they missed the filter by height alone and got the full 1 mm: on the UART mouth, the mouth's top corner chamfer ran from (53.30, 26.77) to (54.30, 25.77), i.e. **0.72 mm past the top pad's edge in the pocket-wall plane**. It removed only skirt — the facet sits entirely at x ≥ 53.30 while the pad is x 45.05 → 53.30, so the pad kept all 2.50 mm around its bore — but it read as a bitten-off pad corner in the viewer. Raising the ceiling drops both mouths' chamfers: 6 faces, +26.4 mm³.
- **The pocket rim stays sharp** (`against_glass`). A 1 mm chamfer there opens the pocket by 1 mm a side, so the 0.5 mm fit gap reads as a 2.5 mm bevelled shadow all the way round the glass. Dropping it is exactly 4 faces and 177.2 mm³ (351.8 mm of pocket perimeter × 0.5 mm²).
- **The outer rim's own perimeter stays sharp too now** (`on_outer_rim`), for `screen_base`'s side panels: they press flush against this face over most of its run to hide the USB-C openings, off `wedge_width` with a slight interference (`screen_base`'s `side_panel_fit`). A 1 mm chamfer there used to recede the wedge behind that flat panel face, opening a visible reveal along the join instead of a flush line.
- USB-C and UART channels run from the pocket wall through the border and **out the outer face** (`outer_wall` 0), as well as through the rear plate. The 2 mm leftover wall was retired so a wrapping base can still reach the plugs from the side with the screen seated. Raise `outer_wall` to close the skirt again.
- **The connector choice is what sizes this part.** It is built around a bare AliExpress right-angle USB-C plug: metal shell + solder PCB, no overmould, so `usbc_plug_shell_width` 8.34 mm straight off the USB-C spec — no wider than the socket it plugs into. That is what let `cable_slot_width` fall 14.5 → 9.6, `cable_slot_depth` 16 → 7, `border_side` 20 → 10, and the part 146 → 126 mm wide. A Delock (20×13×8) or Renkforce overmoulded adapter **does not fit any more** and would need those four numbers back up.
- `outer_wall` 0 opens the outer face. The old 2 mm leftover (and the 0.5 mm slack before that) is a slider, not the default: a wrapping base will hide these sides, and the through openings are how the plugs are reached with the screen seated.
- `border_top_bottom` is 5 mm and is **structural only**: the module already carries its own black bezel on the glass (LCD 54.36 in a 67.80 glass — about 9 mm below, 4 mm above), so the printed border adds nothing visually.
- The skirt is not solid in the print: 57 830 mm³ of CAD volume slices to 36 g where solid PLA would be 72 g. A 4.5 mm border is 1.68 mm of perimeters and the rest infill, so its stiffness comes from the perimeters and the 16.8 mm height, not the thickness.
- Screw holes are M2.5 medium clearance (2.9 mm) with ISO 4762 head counterbore (4.5+0.4 mm), mouths on the bed.
- Measurements came from the Waveshare drawing plus a STEP of the module that is no longer in the repo. Ask the user for any cote you need rather than hunting for the file.
- **To verify on the real board**: `module_rear_hardware` says 7.4 mm stands behind the PCB while the standoffs are 4 mm, so something reaches down to z = 3.4. It clears the 2.5 mm rear plate by **0.9 mm** since `seat_height` went to 4.3 (was 0.6). Raise `seat_height` further if it fouls — but re-read the screw note above first, because every 0.1 mm there is 0.1 mm off the thread engagement.
- **The two sockets in the bottom face are the whole joint to `screen_base`.** They are
  square, not round: in this print pose the bottom face is a vertical wall, so a round
  socket would be a horizontal bore printing out of round at its crown. A square one
  roofs itself with a 5.5 mm bridge and the fit is free anyway. `foot_hole_depth` 3.5
  leaves 1.0 mm behind them in a 4.5 mm border, and `reject` guards that.
- The sockets are a **free fit** (5.5 on a 5 mm pin) on purpose: two pins 60 mm apart on
  a separately printed part will never meet a snug fit.
- **The pocket is 0.5 mm narrower than the drawing said, and the clearance is no longer
  square.** With the real module in hand the fit was 0.5 mm loose across the width, so
  `module_clearance` split into `module_clearance_width` **0.25** and
  `module_clearance_height` 0.5. Pocket 107.10 → **106.60** wide, height unchanged at
  68.80. **No outside dimension moved** and **no screw moved**: the four holes are on the
  module's own 98.00 mount grid, which is measured, not derived from the pocket. What
  moved is `pad_x`, 8.50 → 8.25, because it is computed to leave exactly 2.5 mm of PETG
  around the Ø2.9 bore from the pocket wall inwards — so the pad still gives 2.50 mm
  inboard and now 2.85 mm outboard. `frame_x` (45.05) and the 1.50 mm around the head
  pocket are independent of `pocket_w` and did not move either. The channels' outer wall
  went 2.40 → 2.65 mm.
- **The PCB is 0.8 mm taller than the glass, all of it on the bottom edge, and the pocket
  is sized to the PCB.** So the glass alone would float in a hole 0.8 mm too tall at the
  bottom. `glass_lip_depth` 0.8 puts a lip on the bottom pocket wall in the glass band
  only (`glass_lip_height` 1.0, from the rim down to z 18.60): the module goes in **at an
  angle, bottom first**, the PCB passes under the lip, and the glass then lands against it
  with the same 0.5 mm it has on the other three sides. The lip runs the full 106.60 of
  the pocket and its top face is part of the visible frame rim, which is why it is not
  interrupted over the cable relief.
- **`glass_lip_height` cannot grow past 7.8.** The PCB's front face is at z 10.80
  (`rim_z` − `module_glass_to_pcb`), and the lip has to stop at least 1 mm above it or
  there is nothing for the board to tilt under. `reject` guards it.
- **`nurb check` warns about the lip and the slicer disagrees.** The finding reads
  "107 mm bridge over 96.1 mm²" at (3.8, −34.1, 18.6) — that is the lip's underside, and
  the rule sees a face that lands on the pocket wall at both ends. It is not a span: it is
  a **0.8 mm ledge on a vertical wall** (1.4 mm over the 18 mm where the cable relief is
  under it, 0.8 mm elsewhere — 96.1 mm² is exactly 88.6 × 0.8 + 18 × 1.4). Sliced on the
  A1 Mini it comes out as **58 Overhang wall / 44 Bridge / 98 Floating vertical shell**
  against 56 / 40 / 95 for the part without the lip, `enable_support = 0` and **zero
  support features in the gcode**. Cost: 1 h 01 → **1 h 02**, 31 → **32 g**.
- **The bottom skirt is thinned 0.6 mm where the LCD's flat cable wraps the panel edge.** The cable folds round the 5 mm LCD stack (1 mm glass, then 5 mm of LCD, then the PCB at 8.80) and stands proud of the PCB outline. The 67.80 on the drawing is the **PCB**, not the panel: the real board's glass is 0.8 mm shorter and the difference is all on this edge, which is the room Waveshare left for exactly this cable (see the lip above). So the pocket's 0.50 mm at the bottom is 0.50 mm on the PCB, and the relief takes it to **1.10 mm on the PCB** over 18 mm, centred on the yellow CAN connector at 19.30 in from the **USB-C / UART edge**, so at x +33.75 with its back wall at y −35.00, from z 13.60 to 18.60. Volume cost: 54.0 mm³, and no outside dimension moves.
- **The cable is on the connector side of the board, confirmed against the real module.** It was modelled from the far edge first and mirrored; the parameter is `cable_relief_from_usb_edge` precisely so nobody has to re-derive which way round it goes. A mirror leaves size, volume and face count identical, so `nurb diff` cannot catch this one — check the x of the relief faces in `nurb inspect` instead, it should be **+33.75** and not −33.75.
- **The relief is 18 mm wide for a 15 mm cable, on purpose.** The cable is a lozenge and 15 mm is only its width where it stands proudest, so tracking that number exactly would put the wall back at the PCB line right where the cable is still thick. The extra 3 mm costs 9.0 mm³ and buys 1.5 mm of margin each side, which also absorbs any error in the 19.30.
- **The top 1 mm of frame stays full thickness above the relief** (`cable_relief_below_rim`). That millimetre is the glass thickness, so the glass still lands on an unbroken rim and the frame line does not break where the relief is. It prints as a **0.60 mm overhang** over an 18 mm run, which is why this is a straight notch and not the 45° ramp that was on the table.
- **0.60 mm is where the depth was measured to, not guessed.** Slicing 0.0 / 0.4 / 0.6 / 1.0 on the A1 Mini profile: at 0.4 the gcode is feature-for-feature identical to the part with no relief at all (40 Bridge, 56 Overhang wall), at 0.6 exactly **one** wall segment reclassifies from "floating vertical shell" to "overhang wall" — the slicer slows and cools it and asks for no support — and at 1.0 it is 58 overhang walls and 99 floating shells. Time and weight do not move at any of them (1 h 07, 36.8–36.9 g). So 0.6 is free and 1.0 is where it starts to cost. The innermost perimeter of that lip layer is laid 0.21 mm off the face, so at 0.6 it hangs entirely over air across the 18 mm while at 0.4 it still grazes the wall below; expect a fraction-of-a-layer droop there, on the lip the glass edge meets.
- **The relief clears the foot sockets by 1.05 mm in Z, and that is the only reason it can be a plain notch.** The sockets top out at z 12.55 and only 1.00 mm of border stands behind them; had the relief reached them it would have left 0.40 mm. `reject` on `cable_relief_height` guards it.
- `screen_base` is the cradle this drops into. It backs all 77.8 mm of this part, so a
  press on the glass is compression into the slope rather than a lever on the mount.
- **`magnet_x`/`magnet_y` are `screen_base`'s own magnet-well position, carried through
  `screen_assembly`'s seat transform.** The wells sit right on the seat plane
  (`screen_base`'s boss face is built to lie on it exactly), so any point on that face
  maps straight through the transform to a fixed `(x_w, y_w)` here with `z_w = 0` — no
  reasoning about angles twice. This only holds at `screen_assembly`'s current defaults
  (tilt 45°, seat_height 5); the wedge still takes neither parameter (see Don't), so the
  pairing is a fixed number, not a live one — moving either slider desyncs it.
- **The well stops flush at `rear_wall`, not past it.** Cutting even 0.1mm into the
  skirt above reopened the tangent-sliver `screen_base`'s own card warns about (its
  "notch relief" entry): at this Y the skirt is partly solid, partly already void (the
  pocket boundary runs right through the well's footprint), and any cut reaching past
  `rear_wall` there re-creates the same degenerate coincident face.
- **`magnet_y` is 1mm down-slope from `screen_base`'s own face-midpoint, not the
  midpoint itself.** At the midpoint the well straddles the pocket boundary
  (`pocket_h/2`) by 0.07mm — a sliver, confirmed by `nurb inspect --render`. 1mm down
  clears it on both sides: 0.6mm to the ramp's own apex, 0.9mm to the pocket edge.
  `screen_base`'s own hole moved the same 1mm so the two stay concentric.

## Don't

- Don't interrupt the glass lip over the cable relief "to keep the overhang at 0.6". The
  lip's top face is part of the visible frame rim, so a gap in it is an 18 mm notch in the
  bottom frame line. The continuous lip costs 2 overhang-wall segments, 1 minute and 1 g,
  and asks for no support.
- Don't run the glass lip deeper than the glass. It is 1.0 mm tall on purpose: below the
  glass is the LCD stack and then the PCB at 8.80, and the whole point of the lip is that
  the board slides under it.
- Don't answer the `overhang` warning on the lip with supports or a ramp. It is a 0.8 mm
  ledge the rule reads as a 107 mm span; the gcode is the number, and it has no supports.
- Don't drop the cable relief 0.8 mm (`cable_relief_below_rim` 1.8 / `cable_relief_height`
  4.2) to leave full material under the whole lip. Tried 2026-08-19: the warning stays
  (107 mm, area 96.1 → 85.3 mm², which is just 106.60 × 0.8) because the rule is about the
  **span**, not the depth, and the gcode is **byte-for-byte the same classification** —
  58 Overhang wall / 44 Bridge / 98 Floating vertical shell, 1 h 02 / 32 g, identical. The
  innermost perimeter of that layer is laid 0.21 mm off the face, so it already hangs
  entirely over air at 0.8; the extra 0.6 over 18 mm adds no reclassified segment. It
  would cost the top 0.8 mm of relief, right where the nappe is least measured, for
  nothing.
- Don't put `module_clearance_width` back to 0.5 to match the height. The 0.25 is a
  caliper reading on the real module, not a rounding — the drawing's 106.10 is wide.
- Don't widen `module_clearance_height` to make room for the flat cable. The cable is 15 mm of one edge; opening the whole pocket would give away the fit on the other 335 mm of perimeter to solve it, and the 0.40 mm on the PCB is what makes the module sit without rattling.
- Don't run the relief up through the rim "to avoid the overhang". The overhang is 0.60 mm and prints; the notch in the visible frame line would not come out.
- Don't drop the relief down to the seat. It only has to cover the 5 mm the cable wraps, and going lower walks into the foot sockets, which have 1.00 mm behind them.
- Don't chamfer inside the relief (`in_relief`). The 1 mm polish is larger than the 0.60 mm feature it would be chamfering, and the module hides all of it anyway.
- Don't take `cable_relief_depth` past 0.6 without reslicing. 1.0 is where the slicer starts spreading overhang walls (56 → 58) and floating shells (95 → 99); 0.6 costs exactly one reclassified segment.
- Don't close the outer face back (`outer_wall` 2). Tried and retired: the leftover wall was so the skirt stayed continuous, but a wrapping base will hide these sides and the through openings are how the plugs are reached with the screen seated. Raise the slider only if that base never happens.
- Don't chamfer the channel mouths, and don't answer a chamfer that crowds the top pad by aligning the mouth to the pad instead. Moving the mouth from y 25.77 to 26.05 does not remove the chamfer — the corner stays convex, so `polish` bevels it 0.28 mm higher and the biseau then runs a full 1 mm into the pad's band instead of 0.72. It also spends the 0.28 mm of margin `reject` guards, for a channel that already gives 1.26 mm of total play on an 8.34 mm plug. The fix is the `buried` ceiling, not the opening.
- Don't grow the seat pads back to a 9 mm square "for strength". It is what put a pad across the UART opening, and it buys nothing: the doctrine's own rule is a fastener diameter of wall, which the current 8.35 × 8.25 already gives.
- Don't try to fix the pad/channel collision by shrinking the pads alone. It is worth **0.65 mm** (25.40 → 26.05) and the bare socket alone already reaches 25.47. The fix was the connector, not the pad.
- Don't put the 1 mm of plate back around the pads "to protect the screws". The plate around the head pocket sits below the shoulder and carries nothing; the pads take their strength from the skirt. It is 701 mm³ that buys 1.5 → 2.5 mm on an unloaded wall.
- Don't try to reach the connectors by enlarging the rear opening alone. The pads are on the same band as the PCB edge, so any frame cut to them leaves 9.00 mm of plate over the connectors. Only the notch opens them.
- Don't run the connector notch past the pocket wall at x −53.30. What is beyond it is the 9.5 mm rail tying the skirt to the rear plate on that side, and unlike the USB-C side no channel cuts it.
- Don't delete the rear-plate strip between the rear opening (now x = 45.05) and the pocket wall (x = 53.30) to let an adapter be tilted in. It was considered for the overmoulded Delock; with the bare plug there is nothing to tilt, and that 16.20 mm strip is the only thing tying the skirt to the rear plate on the connector side.
- Don't chamfer the pocket rim, and don't "fix" the sharp edge it leaves. It is deliberate: it is the edge the glass sits against.
- Don't take `seat_height` back to 4.0 to save the 0.3 mm of height. It is what makes an M2.5×8 fit a standoff whose thread depth nobody has measured.
- Don't drop to three pads. It was on the table when the fourth pad fouled the UART channel. The free corner would sit 60 mm from the nearest screw with nothing under it, and a press on the touchscreen there has only the PCB's own stiffness to resist.
- Don't put a plate over the pocket for the glass to sit behind. Tried twice: with the window following the module outline the lip came out 0.1 mm wide, which read as a 68.6 mm hole rim printing on air, a 375.9 mm² bridge over the channels, and finally four floating islands. A real front lip needs the pose flipped, front face on the bed.
- Don't replace the skirt with sparse pillars.
- Don't return the part already rotated to 60° — rotate only in the assembly.
- Don't size the front window to the active pixels; it follows the glass/module outline.
- Don't add a front lip to retain the glass. The module's standoffs and screws hold it, and the four board holes are under the glass anyway, so a lip would only need the pose flipped for nothing.
- Don't sink the skirt into the rear plate with a union before the openings are cut: it refilled the rear opening with a 2664 mm² ceiling.
- Don't cut the magnet well past `rear_wall` "for a clean break", the way the base's own
  through-bore does. There, overshooting clears the bore's angled end cap; here it just
  cuts a sliver of solid skirt at the pocket boundary, since the well's footprint already
  straddles it. Flush at `rear_wall` is correct as is.
- Don't give the wedge its own `tilt`/`seat_height` to derive the magnet position "properly".
  The whole point of this part (see the design notes above and `screen_assembly.md`) is
  that it is the same part at every angle; the magnet pairing already accepts being fixed
  to one configuration instead.

## Changelog

- 2026-09-04: magnet well cut moved onto `system.py`'s new `petit_puit`, and
  `magnet_diameter`'s default raised 5.0 → **5.2mm** (`PETIT_PUIT_DIAMETRE`):
  the magnets would not seat at 5.0, no clearance at all on a 5mm disc.
  `screen_base` shares the same constant for its own (still custom, angled)
  well. Geometry otherwise unchanged — same position, same `rear_wall -
  magnet_cover` depth, still flush at `rear_wall`.
- 2026-09-04: two magnet wells cut into the rear plate, facing `screen_base`'s own pair
  through 0.6mm (`magnet_cover`) a side once seated — a magnet glued in from the pocket
  side, `rear_wall - magnet_cover` (1.9mm) deep. Position (`magnet_x`, `magnet_y`) is
  `screen_base`'s own well carried through `screen_assembly`'s seat transform at its
  current defaults; moved 1mm down-slope from that face's exact midpoint to clear a
  0.07mm sliver at the pocket boundary (see the design notes). `min_wall = 0.6` added to
  this card's settings for the deliberately thin cover. 132 → 136 faces, checks unchanged
  (still the one accepted `overhang` on the glass lip).
- 2026-09-04: outer rim perimeter dropped from the polish pass (`on_outer_rim`),
  so it lands flush against `screen_base`'s new side panels instead of leaving a
  chamfered reveal along the join. Outside dimensions unchanged.
- 2026-09-02: USB-C / UART channels punch through the outer face
  (`outer_wall` 2 → **0**). Same Y and Z as before (9.6 wide, roofed at the
  PCB back z 10.80); the cut now runs to x 63.05 instead of stopping 2.65 mm
  short. No outside dimension moved: still 126.10 × 77.80 × 19.60. Volume
  53 165.9 → 52 606.8 mm³ (−1.1 %). Checks still one `overhang` warn on the
  glass lip; the two new channel roofs are 84 mm² / 9.6 mm span at z 10.80,
  under the printer's 30 mm bridge, plus a 45° polish on the outer lintel.
